english: He often went to the airport.
tip: Repeated trips by vehicle use the multidirectional ездил (yezdil = went): часто ездил (chasto yezdil) means going there regularly, round trip.

target: Он часто водил детей в магазин.
english: He often took the children to the store.
tip: водил (vodil = took) is the multidirectional form for leading someone somewhere repeatedly, unlike the one-way ведёт (vedyot).

english: He is taking the children to school.
tip: везёт (vezyot = is taking) is the unidirectional form for transporting by vehicle in progress, right now toward one place.

english: Mom is taking the child to kindergarten.
tip: ведёт (vedyot = is leading) is the unidirectional form for taking someone on foot to one place now, unlike repeated водит (vodit).

target: Она ездила в Петербург на поезде.
english: She went to St. Petersburg by train.
tip: Means of transport uses на (na = on) plus the prepositional: на поезде (na poezde = by train).

target: Чем больше читаешь, тем умнее становишься.
english: The more you read, the smarter you become.
tip: The more, the more pairs чем (chem) with тем (tem): чем больше читаешь, тем умнее (chem bolshe chitaesh, tem umneye = the more you read, the smarter).

target: Тысяча девятьсот девяносто первый год был важным.
english: The year nineteen ninety-one was important.
tip: In compound years only the last word takes the ordinal ending: девяносто первый (devyanosto pervyy = ninety first), earlier parts stay cardinal.

target: Сестра редко ездит на работу на машине.
english: The sister rarely commutes to work by car.
tip: Traveling by car uses на (na = on) plus the prepositional: на машине (na mashine = by car).

target: Альпинист достиг вершины после восьми часов восхождения.
english: The mountaineer reached the summit after eight hours of climbing.
tip: достичь (dostich = to reach) governs the genitive, not the accusative: достиг вершины (dostig vershiny = reached the summit).

target: Мы убирались, но так и не доделали до конца.
english: We were cleaning, but never finished it.
tip: так и не (tak i ne = never did) plus a perfective marks a planned action that never got done: так и не доделали (tak i ne dodelali = never finished it).

target: Он учил стихотворение, но так и не выучил.
english: He was learning the poem, but never learned it by heart.
tip: Imperfective учил (uchil = studied) names the effort; perfective выучил (vyuchil = learned) names the result, here denied by так и не (tak i ne).

target: Каменотёс обтёсывал гранитный блок молотком и зубилом.
english: The stonemason chipped the granite block with hammer and chisel.
tip: The tool used takes the instrumental with no preposition: молотком и зубилом (molotkom i zubilom = with hammer and chisel).

english: Where are you going?
tip: Куда (kuda = where to) asks about direction with motion verbs, unlike где (gde = where) for a fixed location.

english: The door opens automatically.
tip: The -ся on открывается (otkryvaetsya = opens) makes it intransitive: the door opens by itself, no object needed.

english: He was transporting cargo home.
tip: вёз (vyoz) is past of везти (vezti = carry by vehicle), used when the load moves by transport, not carried by hand.

english: They kiss goodbye.
tip: The -ся on целуются (tseluyutsya = kiss) is reciprocal: they kiss each other, not themselves.

english: We left the party.
tip: A place entered with на (na) is exited with с (s), not из (iz): с вечеринки (s vecherinki = from the party).

english: Birds fly over the lake.
tip: над (nad = over) takes the instrumental case: над озером (nad ozerom = over the lake).

english: We were going to the market.
tip: шли (shli = were going) comes from идти (idti), the one-direction verb for a single trip toward рынок (rynok = market).

english: He often ran to work.
tip: часто (chasto = often) triggers the round-trip verb: бегал (begal = ran there and back), not one-way бежал (bezhal).

english: She wears glasses every day.
tip: носить (nosit) means carry, but with очки (ochki = glasses) or clothes it means wear: носит очки (nosit ochki = wears glasses).

english: He helped me every day.
tip: помогать (pomogat) takes the dative, so the person helped is мне (mne = me), not accusative: помогал мне (pomogal mne = helped me).

english: Why were you late for work?
tip: Being late uses опоздать (opozdat) with на (na) plus accusative: опоздал на работу (opozdal na rabotu = late for work).

english: Who did you call last night?
tip: звонить (zvonit) takes the dative, so the person you call stands in dative and the question word is кому (komu = to whom), as in звонил (zvonil).

english: He doesn't have enough free time.
tip: не хватает (ne khvataet = lacks) is impersonal: the person is dative ему (emu = to him) and the missing thing is genitive времени (vremeni = time).

english: He brought a friend to visit.
tip: в гости (v gosti = for a visit) is a fixed phrase for going to visit someone, used here with привёл (privyol = brought).

english: We need six hundred grams of cheese.
tip: After a large number the noun goes genitive plural: шестьсот граммов (shestsot grammov = six hundred grams).

english: She gets upset because of bad news.
tip: из-за (iz-za = because of) marks a negative cause and takes the genitive: из-за новостей (iz-za novostey = because of the news).

target: Они ездят на работу на метро.
english: They commute to work by metro.
tip: For transport, на (na) plus the prepositional case means by that vehicle: на метро (na metro = by metro).

target: Помоги маме приготовить ужин сегодня вечером.
english: Help mom cook dinner this evening.
tip: Помоги (pomogi = help) is the informal command of помочь (pomoch), the ты (ty) form used with friends, family, or children.
